newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Uraco falls on CAM news.
newsitem.headline: Uraco falls on CAM news.

text.p: Uraco Holdings Ltd shares fell more than six percent, or six cents, to Singapore $0.89 on Monday in speculative trading, dealers said.
Shares in the electronics-based company touched a low of S$0.885 before firming slightly. Volume was a brisk 1.8 million.
A dealer with a local bank said the selling was linked to Uraco's stake in CAM International Holdings, which reported that its auditors had sent a report to the Finance Ministry.
Uraco bought a 6.3 percent stake in CAM last year.
CAM said in a statement it had not seen a copy of the report, but assumed the auditors were worried about possible fraud. The statment said the company was not aware fraud against it.
"The CAM news is probably a trigger for selling. But there is no fundamental reason for the selling," said an analyst with a foreign firm.
Analysts said Uraco's investment in CAM was not significant and should not affect the company's bottom line.
"The share price should recover. But I don't expect Uraco to perform as there is a large block out there waiting to be sold," said the analyst.
Uraco managing director Lim Ee Ann, who holds 17 percent of the company, left the company earlier this year. Analysts said they expected him to sell the shares eventually.
